text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"NJ","level":"state","category":"screening_restrictions","status":"in_force","title":"Fair Chance in Housing Act","requirement":"Housing providers may not ask about an applicant's criminal record, orally or in writing, or use an application form that does so, before making a conditional offer. The only exceptions are methamphetamine manufacture on federally assisted housing premises and lifetime sex-offender registration. Whether before or after a conditional offer, providers may not evaluate applicants on arrests or charges without conviction, expunged, pardoned, vacated or sealed records, or juvenile adjudications. After a conditional offer, only these records may be considered: convictions for listed serious offenses (murder, aggravated sexual assault, kidnapping, arson, human trafficking, etc.) or any crime requiring lifetime sex-offender registration; first-degree indictable offenses within the prior 6 years; second- or third-degree within the prior 4 years; fourth-degree within the prior 1 year. A conditional offer may be withdrawn only if withdrawal is necessary to fulfill a substantial, legitimate, nondiscriminatory interest, shown by a preponderance of the evidence, after an individualized assessment of six factors. The provider must give written notice stating the specific reasons and an opportunity to appeal. The applicant may request the information relied on within 30 days, and the provider must supply it free of charge within 10 days. Before accepting an application fee, the provider must disclose in writing whether criminal history is considered and that the applicant may submit evidence of inaccuracies or rehabilitation. Providers may not require drug or alcohol tests or consent to obtain drug treatment facility records, and may not advertise blanket exclusions of applicants with arrests or convictions. Enforcement is by complaint to the Division on Civil Rights, not in court.","key_value":"Look-back after conditional offer: 6 years (1st degree), 4 years (2nd/3rd degree), 1 year (4th degree); no inquiry before a conditional offer","coverage_conditions":"Applies to housing providers offering rental dwelling units for residential purposes.","exemptions":"Excludes a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units.","coverage_logic":{"covers":null,"exempt":{"all":[{"field":"owner_occupied","op":"==","value":true},{"field":"units","op":"<=","value":4}]}},"subject":"landlord","interaction":null,"yields_to_local":false,"preempts_local":false,"effective_date":"2022-01-01","effective_rule":{"type":"first_day_of_nth_month_after","n":7,"enacted":"2021-06-18"},"enacted_date":"2021-06-18","end_date":null,"penalty":"Monetary penalty up to $1,000 (first violation), $5,000 (one other violation in 5 years), $10,000 (two or more other violations in 7 years); the director may also require cease and desist, return of the application fee, or payment of up to $1,000 to the applicant.","citation":"P.L.2021, c.110 (N.J.S.A. 46:8-52 to 46:8-64)","quoted_span":"A housing provider shall not make any oral or written inquiry regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.","supporting_spans":["This act shall take effect on the first day of the seventh month next following the date of enactment","“Rental dwelling unit” means a dwelling unit offered for rent by a housing provider for residential purposes, other than a dwelling unit in an owner-occupied premises of not more than four dwelling units."],"confidence":0.95,"conflict_note":null}],"notes":"Only one in-scope category applies (screening_restrictions). The application-fee provision is a disclosure requirement rather than a fee cap, so it is folded into the screening rule. Effective date computed as the first day of the 7th month after approval on 2021-06-18, which is 2022-01-01."}
